explanations: rag_llm-The NCBI accession record explicitly states 'country: cambodia'. The geographic location is confirmed throughout the paper as Cambodia, with samples collected from "three provinces in northeastern Cambodia" per the Methods section. The publication title and study design consistently identify Cambodia as the geographic location. [Sources: NCBI_accession (country field, 'cambodia'); https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3599 (Methods section, 'three provinces in northeastern Cambodia')] [Conflict: none] [ID-match: true]

rag_llm-Sample KC505116 originates from a living individual (blood sample collected 02-OCT-2013). The isolation_source is listed as "aboriginal" in the NCBI record, referring to the ethnic/population category (Brao aboriginal population), not to temporal context. The sample type is biological material (mitochondrial DNA from blood) from a modern living person, not an ancient or archaeological specimen. [Sources: NCBI_accession (isolation_source: 'aboriginal'; collection_date: '02-OCT-2013'); https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3599 (Methods, 'blood samples from...living individuals')] [Conflict: none] [ID-match: true]

rag_llm-The sample isolate identifier is "Brao02_N7", where "Brao" refers to the Brao ethnic group, one of the 13 aboriginal populations sampled in the study. The paper's Methods section lists populations studied: "1. Brao; 2. Jarai; 3. Kachac..." The Brao population is explicitly identified as one of the aboriginal Mon-Khmer/Austro-Asiatic speaking groups from northeastern Cambodia. Sample KC505116 belongs within the accession range KC505067–KC505122, which corresponds to wholegenome sequences from 98 selected Cambodian individuals. The "Brao02" designation indicates the second Brao individual in the sequenced subset. [Sources: NCBI_accession (isolate: 'Brao02_N7'); https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3599 (Methods section, 'Numbers refer to the populations (1. Brao; 2. Jarai; 3. Kachac...' and 'representing 13 aboriginal ethnic populations')] [Conflict: none] [ID-match: true]

organism.explanation: NCBI GenBank record and BioSample metadata both specify organism as Homo sapiens. [Sources: NCBI_accession (all_features, 'organism: Homo sapiens'), web_search_https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/KC505116/ (record title, 'Homo sapiens')]

isolate.explanation: BioSample attribute isolate is Brao02_N7, consistent across NCBI accession metadata and GenBank record. [Sources: NCBI_accession (isolate: 'Brao02_N7'), https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3599 (Methods, '98 Cambodian individuals')]

geo_loc_name.explanation: BioSample attribute geo_loc_name specifies Cambodia; paper Methods and Results sections confirm samples from Cambodia. [Sources: NCBI_accession (geo_loc_name: 'Cambodia'), https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3599 (Methods, 'We collected 5 ml of blood samples from a total of 1,054 unrelated individuals...from Cambodia')]

collection_date.explanation: BioSample metadata provides collection_date as 02-OCT-2013. [Sources: NCBI_accession (collection_date: '02-OCT-2013')]

isolation_source.explanation: NCBI GenBank all_features attribute specifies isolation_source as aboriginal. [Sources: NCBI_accession (all_features, 'isolation_source: aboriginal')]

sample_type.explanation: Paper Methods section explicitly states blood samples were collected: 'We collected 5 ml of blood samples'. [Sources: https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3599 (Methods, 'We collected 5 ml of blood samples')]

mol_type.explanation: NCBI GenBank all_features specify mol_type as genomic DNA. [Sources: NCBI_accession (all_features, 'mol_type: genomic DNA')]

organelle.explanation: NCBI GenBank all_features and record title specify mitochondrion as the organelle being sequenced. [Sources: NCBI_accession (all_features, 'organelle: mitochondrion'), web_search_https://www.ncbi.nlm.nih.gov/nuccore/KC505116/ (record title, 'mitochondrion, complete genome')]

population.explanation: Paper Methods section indicates this sample belongs to the Brao ethnic population, identified from the isolate name Brao02_N7 and confirmed in population table references. [Sources: https://doi.org/10.1038/ncomms3599 (Results, 'Population abbreviations: Br, Brao')]
